meta.question: E34 localized the DNA-damage ratio's out-of-band-ness to the concentrated 21x21 straight-fibre grid inflating indirect. Does re-scoring the same dump against realistic chromatin geometry (analytical nucleosome->fibre) lower the ratio?
meta.method: Dual-geometry scoring: same Auger v0.7.0 dump; direct = rad_dep energy-threshold, indirect = 633,979 surviving-OH positions (1us, collected via the worker collectOH hook) with P_indirect=0.13. Both geometries at matched bp (3.89M) in the same +/-1500 nm region. src/physics/chromatin-geometry.ts + experiments/tools/chromatin-score.cjs.

finding: Realistic chromatin geometry LOWERS the indirect/direct ratio (2.12 -> 1.68) vs the straight grid — directional support for E34: the ratio is geometry-dependent and the concentrated grid inflates indirect relative to direct.
caveats: Survival-OH indirect model (P=0.13 per near sugar), NOT the worker's full ssb_indirect (which also scores at reaction events) — so absolute numbers differ from the production ratio 5.74; the grid-vs-chromatin comparison is valid because both use the identical model.

The chromatin fibres are randomly scattered in the 3 um box, so many miss the concentrated track core (99% of dose in the central few um, E12-local) -> both absolute counts drop (a sampling artifact). A rigorous quantitative comparison needs dose-matched placement (chromatin where the track deposits energy) + a proper nuclear dose normalisation.
Chromatin packs DNA ~27x denser than straight B-DNA (80 vs 3 bp/nm), so 'matched bp + matched region' cannot also match spatial extent.
status: pass (first-order) — geometry infrastructure validated end-to-end (nucleosome/fibre -> spatial hash -> dual scoring); directional evidence that realistic chromatin lowers the ratio (E34 confirmed in direction). Rigorous dose-matched version is future work.
